title: ready-01: heca as a library, with an entry point for adding things
summary: The heca crate becomes library + small main.rs; another crate can add actions, docks, pane decorations and overlays at startup.
description:
heca-pro uses heca's crates as Cargo git dependencies (decision 1 in `~/projects/heca-pro/docs/decisions.md`). For that, the `heca` crate must also be a library.

## Current state
- `heca/Cargo.toml:2` — program only, no `[lib]`.
- `HecaApp` (private) in `heca/src/main.rs:50`; `fn main` at :475; app setup in `heca/src/app/startup.rs`.
- Actions are registered in the ActionCatalog (`heca/src/actions/`); docks come from providers (`heca/src/providers/`, e.g. the workspaces dock); overlays/layers from `heca/src/chrome/`.

## Goal
- `heca/src/lib.rs` exposes the app; `main.rs` shrinks to a few lines calling it. **The `heca` program builds and runs exactly as today.**
- One public entry point (a builder on the app) where another crate adds, before the app starts: actions, docks (providers), pane decorations, overlays. Write it as the line a plugin author would type — no registry ids, no crate-private types. It is the same opening the plugin system needs; reuse the provider/ActionCatalog paths, never a second one.
- heca-pro can then depend on heca pinned to a tag/commit, with a local path override for working on both.

## Preserve
- Every current behaviour of the `heca` binary; all tests green.
- AGENTS.md § 0/0b/0d; no hard-coded placement — a heca-pro dock is placed by the user like any dock.

## Done when
- A tiny example crate (or test) builds an app through the entry point, adds one action and one dock, and both work (action reachable by key, menu and RPC; dock placeable in either sidebar).

tasks.description:
Execution task for P098. Read the phase description first, and `~/projects/heca-pro/docs/architecture.md` ("Two editions, one code base underneath").

Current: `heca/Cargo.toml:2` program only; `HecaApp` private at `heca/src/main.rs:50`; `fn main` at :475; startup in `heca/src/app/startup.rs`; actions in the ActionCatalog (`heca/src/actions/`); docks from providers (`heca/src/providers/`).

Steps are in the checklist. Design the entry point first and agree it with Antonio before writing it (it is a public API a plugin author will also read) — write the line a plugin author would type. Edge cases: the binary must not change behaviour; tests that reach private items keep working; nothing heca-pro adds may need a registry id.
